core_insight: Authorization is a gatekeeper decision of Principal + Action + Resource + Context → Allow/Deny, and it should be separated from enforcement so policy can change without code deploys.

scenes.voice: You know who you are. But can you actually do this?
scenes.visual: Split screen: left shows login success 'Authenticated', right shows API call blocked with 'Forbidden'.

scenes.voice: Authentication answers who are you. Authorization answers what are you allowed to do here. The problem starts when one API serves many users, tenants and roles.
scenes.visual: One API box with multiple users, tenants, roles arrows pointing in. Highlight scattered if user.role == 'admin' code snippets.

scenes.voice: Hard-coding checks across services creates drift and security holes. You need consistent decisions without coupling business logic to permission logic.
scenes.visual: Three services each with duplicated if statements, then a red warning icon for drift.

scenes.voice: Think of it as a bouncer with a list. Auth gives you the ID. Authorization checks principal, action, resource and context against policy.
scenes.visual: Bouncer metaphor with ID card, door label, time stamp, and list.

scenes.voice: Separate enforcement from decision. The API is the Policy Enforcement Point. It asks a Policy Decision Point which reads the Policy Store. The PDP is stateless and never trusts the client, only verified claims plus policy.
scenes.visual: Flow diagram animating request through PEP to PDP to Policy Store and back.
scenes.mermaid:
flowchart LR
    Client -->|Request + Token| API
    API --> PEP[Policy Enforcement Point]
    PEP --> PDP[Policy Decision Point]
    PDP --> PolicyStore[(Policies)]
    PDP -->|Allow/Deny| PEP
    PEP --> Resource

scenes.voice: Centralize policy when it changes faster than code and is shared. Push checks in-process only when policy is stable and latency is critical.
scenes.visual: Scale balancing 'Change velocity & shared model' vs 'Latency & simple policy'.

scenes.voice: You gain consistency and auditability, you pay latency and blast radius. Cache short-lived decision tokens, version policies, and design for PDP failure.
scenes.visual: Checkmarks for consistency, audit, then warning icons for latency, blast radius, stale cache.

mental_model: Authorization is Principal + Action + Resource + Context → Allow/Deny enforced by a PEP that asks a stateless PDP. Keep enforcement separate from decision so policy can evolve without redeploying services.
final_takeaway: Don't scatter if role checks. Separate enforcement from policy decision and centralize when policy changes faster than code.
